source_metadata.etymology_text: From Old Galician-Portuguese põer (“to put”), from Latin pōnere, from Proto-Italic *pozinō. Cognate of Spanish poner, French pondre, Italian porre, Sicilian pùniri.
raw_glosses: (transitive, intransitive) to lay (to produce and deposit an egg)

unused_menu_senses.translation: to lay (to produce and deposit an egg)

canonical_example.text: Pusemos blusas para não passarmos/passármos frio.
canonical_example.translation: We put on blouses so we wouldn’t be cold.

source_metadata.etymology_text: From Old Galician-Portuguese põer (“to put”), from Latin pōnere, from Proto-Italic *pozinō. Cognate of Spanish poner, French pondre, Italian porre, Sicilian pùniri.
raw_glosses: (transitive) to put on; to wear (to start to use an item of clothing)

unused_menu_senses.translation: to put on; to wear (to start to use an item of clothing)

source_metadata.etymology_text: Borrowed from French traîner, from Old French trahiner.
